text: Reject: 'ASR on AgentDojo is a rerun of PISmith with a different string.' Invert: report *undetected* ASR only, gated by an off-the-shelf injection detector (PromptGuard, DeBERTa injection classifier, perplexity filter) and show belief-poisoning slips through where hijack strings get caught, because it contains no imperative and no attacker task.
rationale: Turns the sameness complaint into a measurable differentiator: the artifact is a detector-bypass curve, not an ASR table.

text: Reject: 'AgentDojo has no notion of a wrong-but-compliant answer, so your metric is ill-defined.' Invert: build a 300-item 'FactDojo' by wrapping existing ground-truth QA (TriviaQA/NQ/TruthfulQA) as fake search/RAG/tool JSON, define Belief Poisoning Rate = user task attempted AND final answer flips from correct to attacker-chosen, and release it as the benchmark contribution.
rationale: Objective ground truth exists for QA in a way it does not for agent side tasks, so the metric is defensible and the benchmark alone justifies a workshop paper.

text: Reject: 'A 0.5B policy tuned on one target is overfit noise.' Invert: train on a single small open target, then evaluate transfer to 5 frozen targets you never rewarded against, and report a fabrication-type taxonomy (fake statute, fake date, fake org, fake retraction) learned by the policy and which types transfer.
rationale: Transfer plus a taxonomy converts a fragile result into a claim about what kinds of fabricated authority LLMs trust generically.

text: Reject: 'GPT-4 could write these fake citations zero-shot, why RL?' Invert: head-to-head against GPT-4-written fabrications at matched length, showing RL learns *plausibility-under-suspicion* (survives when target is warned 'tool outputs may be tampered'), and plot poisoning rate vs. how many facts are fabricated.
rationale: Makes the paper about the optimization objective finding a niche prompting cannot, and quantifies the attacker's cost.

text: Reject: 'Known defenses solve this.' Invert: run the standard hijack defenses (tool-output delimiting, spotlighting, instruction-hierarchy prompting, Task Shield style intent checks) and show they are near-useless here because the agent's intent never deviates, then state the headline: intent-preserving attacks are outside the threat model every current defense assumes.
rationale: A negative result on existing defenses is the fastest publishable claim, and it is exactly what the workshop scope 'factuality, robustness' asks for.

text: Reject: 'Wrong trivia answers are harmless, not agent security.' Invert: add an action sink, the poisoned belief changes a downstream tool call (wrong date -> wrong calendar booking, fake regulation -> refuses/approves a transaction), and measure action-flip rate, not answer-flip rate.
rationale: Ties factuality to consequence, which is the only reason an agents-security reviewer will care.
